title: High-touch onramp playbook for renewal-triggered features
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers approaching renewals have escalated requests for feature work that would materially affect renewal outcomes. Current intake is ad-hoc; engineering sprints and roadmaps do not have a fast, repeatable path for evaluating, costing, and committing to renewal-linked feature asks.

Objective: Create a high-touch onramp playbook and decision flow that converts renewal-triggered customer requests into scoped, timeboxed roadmap commitments or formal trade-off offers within 10 business days of intake. Playbook will be operable by PMs + Solutions Engineers + Sales and implementable without additional headcount.

Success metrics (30/60/90):
- 30 days: Playbook approved by Sales Ops and Legal; two pilot accounts processed end-to-end.
- 60 days: 80% of renewal-triggered asks routed through playbook; median time from intake to proposal <= 7 business days.
- 90 days: Renewal win-rate improvement for pilot cohort >= +12% relative to baseline; at least one feature committed into roadmap release-2026.05.

Scope (in):
- Intake form template for Sales (Google Form + Salesforce event)
- Standardized evaluation rubric (impact, engineering effort, security/compliance, strategic value)
- Costing playbook (trade-offs: scope fractioning, premium delivery window, paid engineering add-on)
- Fast-path approval steps and SLA for decisioning (PM + Eng lead + Legal)
- A template commitment statement (contract language) and handoff to Delivery

Out of scope:
- Long-term product strategy changes (these go through normal roadmap cycles)
- Major architecture rework requiring >3 sprints of dedicated effort (these need executive sign-off)

Approach and tasks:
1) Intake & signal capture: design form + Salesforce mapping + add 'renewal_routing' flag. Owner: Sales Ops. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/renewal-onramp
2) Evaluation rubric: craft quantitative scoring (impact 1-10, revenue delta estimate, engineering T-shirt). Owner: Product. Link to spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Renewal+Onramp+Rubric
3) Rapid costing: engineering micro-estimate checklist and 'accelerate' pricing tiers. Owner: Eng Leads. PR template: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/renewal-costing
4) SLA workflow automation: Slack alerts and a decision board in the Console roadmap workspace. Owner: Program Ops.
5) Pilot with 3 accounts: run full flow, collect qualitative notes and telemetry (renewal outcome).

Acceptance criteria (must be true for Done):
- Intake form integrated into Salesforce and linked in Sales playbook.
- Rubric documented and review-approved by Eng, Legal, Security.
- Two pilot account proposals delivered within SLA and decision recorded in Confluence + Salesforce.
- One approved trade-off or roadmap commit with corresponding JIRA/ENG ticket created and linked.
- Dashboard created showing time-to-decision, estimated revenue impact, and renewal outcome per account.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: Finalize templates and automation; legal sign-off on contract language.
- Week 3-4: Pilot with 3 accounts; iterate on rubric thresholds.
- Week 5: Present pilot learnings to GTM and Exec; recommend scale path.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Dashboard: renewal_onramp/time_to_decision (median), renewal_onramp/win_rate_delta (cohort), renewal_onramp/average_eng_hours_per_commit. Dashboard link: https://datadog.company/internal/dashboards/renewal-onramp

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering capacity overload if multiple pilots align to same release window. Mitigation: capacity hedge (defer to paid expedited delivery or split scope).
- Risk: Legal negotiation delays. Mitigation: pre-authorized clause library and 48-hour legal SLA for pilot lanes.
